candidates_considered.biomedical_relevance: Trained on MS MARCO, not BioASQ. Not domain-adapted. Chosen because it produces sparse term-weight vectors that can match latent terms BM25 never sees, and DistilBERT is small enough to encode 40k passages locally overnight.
candidates_considered.local_inference: CPU or CUDA; DistilBERT MLM (~67M params); no API key
candidates_considered.expected_output: 30522-d sparse vector (WordPiece vocab weights, ReLU + log saturation)
candidates_considered.indexing: CSR document-term matrix; reusable on-disk cache
candidates_considered.license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (Naver SPLADE-v3). Experimental/research use only.
candidates_considered.expected_memory_runtime: Index ~tens of MB sparse CSR for 40k docs. Encode time on CPU similar to or faster than BERT-base PubMedBERT (~minutes, not hours).

candidates_considered.biomedical_relevance: MS MARCO, not BioASQ. Higher MS MARCO quality, slower CPU encode.
candidates_considered.expected_memory_runtime: Slower than DistilBERT; encode cost similar to PubMedBERT (~5–10 min CPU).

candidates_considered.biomedical_relevance: MS MARCO DistilBERT; widely used SPLADE checkpoint.
candidates_considered.expected_output: sparse term weights over WordPiece vocab

candidates_considered.biomedical_relevance: General web/MS MARCO style, not BioASQ. Query encoder is separate (doc-only weights).
candidates_considered.local_inference: Would need a matching query encoder; more plumbing than SPLADE
candidates_considered.expected_memory_runtime: Similar DistilBERT cost, but two-tower setup is extra integration risk overnight.
candidates_considered.rejected_reason: Asymmetric query/doc encoders add integration risk versus a single SPLADE encoder.

candidates_considered.source: Literature search; no drop-in Sentence-Transformers SparseEncoder checkpoint
candidates_considered.biomedical_relevance: Would be preferable if a local, licensed, HF-loadable checkpoint existed.
candidates_considered.rejected_reason: No practical local biomedical SPLADE checkpoint was available to evaluate overnight.

why_this_model: naver/splade-v3-distilbert produces learned sparse term weights, is DistilBERT-sized so 40k passages can be encoded locally, and is trained on MS MARCO rather than this BioASQ eval split (no gold-ID leakage). It is not biomedical-adapted; that is a documented tradeoff.
leakage_note: The sparse encoder is given only query strings and passage text. Gold passage IDs, relevance labels, and reference answers are used after retrieval for scoring and are never passed into encode().
